summary: Tested role-specific signup (all 6 roles, UI + API), Google completion mode, provider document upload/delete, reviewer approve/send-back, ticks on verification page/public profile, hourly disclaimer (Post Job + Book flow), demo logins, email lowercasing, matching-engine regression (iter22 suite) and address search. Backend: 20/20 new tests pass + 22/22 iter22 regression pass; 2 security probes fail (see issues). Frontend: one CRITICAL bug found and fixed by me — new providers (email signup AND Google 'Finish') were sent to /provider/verification?welcome=1 and then immediately bounced to /provider/dashboard -> /provider/onboarding, so the documents step (Step 2 of 3) was skipped. After my fix all UI flows pass.

critical.issue: Any logged-in user can download any file, including a provider's police check / qualification PDFs, if they know the URL. There is no owner/reviewer check. Police-vetting documents are sensitive personal data. Fix: if the file is linked to provider_documents, allow only the owner or is_reviewer(user) (or keep a private flag on files uploaded for documents). Covered by tests/test_iter23_security_probes.py::test_other_user_cannot_read_police_check_file (currently FAILS).

When a customer switches to provider, the provider_profile it creates has verified=True, insured=True and rating=4.7. That skips the new review process. The UI 'Switch Account Type' gives users a way to look verified without a review. Fix: create it with verified/qualified_verified/police_checked/insured=False, rating 0, the same as register. Covered by test_iter23_security_probes.py::test_role_switch_does_not_grant_verified (currently FAILS).

minor.issue: The response user has no is_reviewer field (login, /me, session and complete-signup do include it). This only matters until /me refreshes.

Sets verified = qualified or police. ProviderProfile then shows an 'ID Verified' badge when only a qualification was approved, which is misleading. It also overwrites the legacy 'verified' flag of seeded providers the first time any of their docs is reviewed.

Legacy users with no signup_complete field (e.g. demo accounts) can change their role through this endpoint, because the guard only checks signup_complete truthy. Consider `user.get('signup_complete') is not False`.
'10 Queen Street Auckland' returns Rodney 0910 results first instead of Auckland CBD (relevance only; endpoint works).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: the useEffect `if (user && user.signup_complete !== false) navigate(ROLE_HOME...)` ran after register()/complete-signup set the user. It overrode navigate(afterSignupPath), so providers ended up on /provider/onboarding and never saw the documents step. Fixed with a justSignedUp ref.

integration_issues.flow: AuthCallback (Google) for an EXISTING account clicked from /signup
integration_issues.issue: isNew = !!pending, so an existing user who presses 'Sign up with Google' is routed to afterSignupPath (provider -> verification welcome). Their chosen role/details are silently ignored and no message tells them they already have an account. Not reachable in preview (real Google OAuth), found by code review.
The Approved and Rejected tabs have no actions, so a reviewer cannot revoke an approval or approve a re-check from those tabs. The provider has to upload again.

issues: The Expiry date field uses the browser's native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of the shadcn Calendar/DatePicker
The 'Issued by' and 'Licence / reference number' inputs have no data-testid
The email/password inputs and the submit button have no data-testid

Account type defaults to 'residential' for Facilities in the UI, but the backend default for facilities is 'commercial'. A new facilities user lands on the 'Residential Facilities Portal'. Consider defaulting to commercial for facilities.

rca of the issue: Signup redirect bug: register() and setUser() update AuthContext.user while Signup is still mounted. The 'already signed in' useEffect then fires navigate(ROLE_HOME[role]) after goNext's navigate(afterSignupPath), so the last navigation wins: /provider/dashboard, which redirects not-onboarded providers to /provider/onboarding. Repro: sign up as a provider and watch the URL go verification -> onboarding within about 1s. Mitigation applied: a useRef flag set before register/complete-signup that suppresses the effect redirect.
